subject.title: [Feature]: Optimization for Dockerfile.sandbox-common # add retries and fix-missings for apt-get

question: Should the sandbox Dockerfile fix be retry-only, or may it also use `--fix-missing` with package-presence verification?
rationale: `Acquire::Retries` directly addresses transient APT fetch failures, while apt-get documents `--fix-missing` as holding back packages that cannot be retrieved, so the final behavior is a product/safety choice for sandbox image builds.

options.title: Use retry-only APT commands
options.body: Keep `Acquire::Retries` on update/install, remove `--fix-missing`, and require real build plus package-presence proof before landing.

options.title: Accept `--fix-missing` with verification
options.body: Allow partial-fetch tolerance only if the PR verifies every required package/binary and documents the intended sandbox image contract.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Reject Dockerfile retry changes if maintainers prefer build failures to remain fully governed by upstream APT and CI retries.

recommendation.title: Use retry-only APT commands
recommendation.body: Keep `Acquire::Retries` on update/install, remove `--fix-missing`, and require real build plus package-presence proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: This login introduced the sandbox-common builder, Dockerfile split, and smoke workflow that define the affected setup path.
